scope: Encrypted backup package assembly, atomic file publication and isolated manifest-verified restore staging; not completed daemon backup/restore commands

format.manifest: Length-prefixed UTF-8 JSON metadata/file records, exact file bodies, then counts and SHA-256 of manifest records. Outer authentication is completed explicitly after the final package record.
format.partial: Partial file records contain no body or content hash. Atomically published partial archives end in .partial.sbk.

verifiedBehavior: Incremental encryption supports multiple writes and flushes; disposal without successful explicit completion leaves an unauthenticated archive.
Round-trip verification checks every file size/hash, manifest counts/hash, state migration version, full schema fingerprint, instance id, account epoch, SQLite integrity and foreign keys.
Owned files, trash, external originals and keyring bytes survive a complete encrypted round trip.
Thirty-two real content edits during package writing leave staged restored bytes and state hashes consistent with the captured version.
A real persisted ASP.NET Data Protection and HMAC key ring restores a protected calendar subscription link and verifies an existing signature.
Atomic publication writes 0600 files, syncs the result and containing directory, distinguishes partial archives and removes failed temporary output.

Wrong keys, ciphertext corruption, unsafe paths, duplicate entries, invalid record lengths, missing state, hash/schema mismatches, trailing plaintext and staging limits are rejected; failed restore workspaces are removed.
Restored content is exposed only through a verified private workspace; existing files and external roots are not modified.
notes: The first package run used SQLite user_version for schema metadata, but this repository tracks migrations in migration_state. The package now records that authoritative version and a hash of the complete schema.
The incremental writer requests smaller source read chunks than the original bulk codec; its bounded-read test now checks the maximum rather than requiring an exact allocation size.
The storage test project adds an ASP.NET Core framework reference solely to exercise real persisted Data Protection keys. No production NuGet dependency changed.
Tests use synthetic data, synthetic keys and temporary local stores. No browser workflow or production service changed.
limitations: The daemon use case, admin endpoints/CLI, backup-key provisioning, root selection, and consistent capture of live index/embedding descriptors still need integration.
Verification stages a package; it does not install state/files, remap paths, increment the account epoch or rebuild the running index.
Verified partial packages remain labelled partial; a future installer must enforce its explicit partial-restore policy.
Restore currently authenticates a bounded private plaintext package before extraction, so staging needs capacity for the package and extracted files.
Backup rotation, export, interrupted-workspace recovery, pre-migration snapshots and full hardened-deployment qualification remain open.
The controlled sustained-edit round trip is not full daemon restore acceptance or a large-corpus latency/memory benchmark.
